'Sunday review time,' Charu said, dropping onto Vasudha's bed. 'Show me.'
Vasudha opened her planner. 'Done: stats assignment, two chapters of sociology, laundry. Slipped: the literature essay draft and my Wednesday swim.'
'Why?'
'The essay... I kept starting it at eleven at night. And swimming, I skipped because I'd stayed up for the essay I didn't write.'
Charu laughed. 'So one problem ate two things.'
'Exactly.' Vasudha moved the essay into Monday and Tuesday mornings, two hours each. 'Mornings. Not nights.' Then she looked at the week ahead and frowned. 'Tests on Wednesday and Friday, essay due Friday, and I promised to help at the book drive on Thursday.'
'That's a lot.'
'It's too much. I'll ask Meghna to swap Thursday with me for next week.' She typed the message and hit send. 'There. Done.'

qa.q: Which two things slipped last week?
qa.a: The literature essay draft and the Wednesday swim.

qa.q: How does Vasudha seem to feel after sending the message to Meghna?
qa.a: Vasudha seems relieved and in control, having turned an overfull week into one that fits.

qa.q: What else could Vasudha try if the morning essay slots also slip?
qa.a: Break the essay into one small part per slot, like an outline on Monday, so starting feels easier.

qa.q: How does the Sunday review look to Charu?
qa.a: Charu treats it as a friendly ritual and helps by asking 'why', spotting that one problem ate two things.

grounding: Shows a student reviewing on Sunday what was done, what slipped and why, moving the unfinished essay into next week and swapping out one commitment.
